<section id="working-life-pilot" class="ci-wl" aria-labelledby="wl-title">
<div class="ci-section-heading"><div><p class="ci-eyebrow">TÜRKİYE / FIRST OFFICIAL-DATA PILOT</p><h2 id="wl-title">Working Life · 2025</h2><p>Five published annual observations. Actual percentages, not index scores.</p></div><span class="ci-wl-badge">Official survey estimates · source checked</span></div>
<p class="ci-wl-source">Source: <a href="https://veriportali.tuik.gov.tr/tr/press/57996">TÜİK, <span lang="tr">İşgücü İstatistikleri, 2025</span> · bulletin 57996</a>. Published 25 March 2026; checked 4 November 2026.</p>
<div class="ci-wl-grid"><article class="ci-wl-card"><p class="ci-eyebrow">WL-01 / Core observation</p><h3>Employment rate</h3><p class="ci-wl-value">49.0<span>%</span></p><p class="ci-wl-change">-0.5 percentage points vs 2024</p><p class="ci-wl-age">Age 15+ · total</p><details><summary>Definition and provenance</summary><p>Numerator: Employed people. Denominator: Non-institutional population aged 15+.</p><p>Source section: <span lang="tr">İstihdam oranı</span>.</p><a href="https://veriportali.tuik.gov.tr/tr/press/57996">TÜİK bulletin 57996 ↗</a></details></article><article class="ci-wl-card"><p class="ci-eyebrow">WL-02 / Core observation</p><h3>Unemployment rate</h3><p class="ci-wl-value">8.3<span>%</span></p><p class="ci-wl-change">-0.4 percentage points vs 2024</p><p class="ci-wl-age">Age 15+ · total</p><details><summary>Definition and provenance</summary><p>Numerator: Unemployed people. Denominator: Labour force aged 15+.</p><p>Source section: <span lang="tr">İşsizlik oranı</span>.</p><a href="https://veriportali.tuik.gov.tr/tr/press/57996">TÜİK bulletin 57996 ↗</a></details></article><article class="ci-wl-card"><p class="ci-eyebrow">WL-03 / Core observation</p><h3>Labour underutilisation rate (LU4)</h3><p class="ci-wl-value">29.7<span>%</span></p><p class="ci-wl-change">+3.0 percentage points vs 2024</p><p class="ci-wl-age">Age 15+ · total</p><details><summary>Definition and provenance</summary><p>Numerator: Unemployed people + time-related underemployed people + potential labour force. Denominator: Labour force + potential labour force, aged 15+.</p><p>Source section: <span lang="tr">Atıl işgücü oranı</span>.</p><a href="https://veriportali.tuik.gov.tr/tr/press/57996">TÜİK bulletin 57996 ↗</a></details></article><article class="ci-wl-card"><p class="ci-eyebrow">WL-04 / Context observation</p><h3>Labour force participation rate</h3><p class="ci-wl-value">53.5<span>%</span></p><p class="ci-wl-change">-0.7 percentage points vs 2024</p><p class="ci-wl-age">Age 15+ · total</p><details><summary>Definition and provenance</summary><p>Numerator: Labour force. Denominator: Non-institutional population aged 15+.</p><p>Source section: <span lang="tr">İşgücüne katılma oranı</span>.</p><a href="https://veriportali.tuik.gov.tr/tr/press/57996">TÜİK bulletin 57996 ↗</a></details></article><article class="ci-wl-card"><p class="ci-eyebrow">WL-05 / Context observation</p><h3>Youth unemployment rate</h3><p class="ci-wl-value">15.3<span>%</span></p><p class="ci-wl-change">-1.0 percentage points vs 2024</p><p class="ci-wl-age">Age 15–24 · total</p><details><summary>Definition and provenance</summary><p>Numerator: Unemployed people aged 15–24. Denominator: Labour force aged 15–24.</p><p>Source section: <span lang="tr">Genç nüfusta işsizlik oranı</span>.</p><a href="https://veriportali.tuik.gov.tr/tr/press/57996">TÜİK bulletin 57996 ↗</a></details></article></div>
<p class="ci-wl-reading"><strong>Read the measures together.</strong> Unemployment fell, while labour underutilisation rose and employment and participation declined. A falling unemployment rate alone does not establish an improvement across working life. Percentage-point changes are published comparisons, not percentage growth rates.</p>
<details class="ci-sse-details"><summary>Coverage, calculation and limits</summary><p>The pilot is a release-vintage snapshot, not a live feed or a reconstruction from rounded headcounts. The annual values are taken directly from one official bulletin. No monthly, seasonally adjusted or modelled international series is substituted.</p><p>Population coverage follows the Household Labour Force Survey: non-institutional households. Youth unemployment uses the youth labour force, not all young people. LU4 uses an extended labour-force denominator; see <a href="https://www.ilo.org/sites/default/files/wcmsp5/groups/public/%40dgreports/%40stat/documents/publication/wcms_220535.pdf">ILO measurement framework</a>. The rates have different denominators and must not be added.</p><p>No composite score, rank, weights or normalisation have been assigned. Unemployment is part of labour underutilisation, so equal-weight aggregation would risk double counting. Participation and youth unemployment are context measures here; potential overlap with other dimensions must be reviewed.</p><p>Wages, excessive hours, informal employment and occupational safety are not yet collected in this pilot. It is an initial labour-market view, not full coverage of job quality. Sampling uncertainty and later revisions have not been quantified; published changes are not claims of statistical significance.</p></details>

</section>

<section id="dimensions"><p class="ci-eyebrow">THE PROPOSED FRAMEWORK</p><h2>Six lenses on working life and social policy</h2><p>These dimensions follow the association’s original Index brief. Indicators below are candidates for consultation, not an approved measurement framework.</p><div class="ci-dimension-grid"><article class="ci-dimension"><span class="ci-dimension-number">01</span><h3>Working life</h3><p>Employment, job quality, wages and working conditions.</p><small>First official-data pilot</small><p><strong>Türkiye · 2025 annual observations</strong></p><a href="#working-life-pilot">Explore Working Life →</a></article><article class="ci-dimension"><span class="ci-dimension-number">02</span><h3>Social policy</h3><p>Social protection, social security and access to services.</p><small>Candidate indicator</small><p><strong>Social protection coverage</strong></p></article><article class="ci-dimension"><span class="ci-dimension-number">03</span><h3>Equality and inclusion</h3><p>Participation and opportunity across population groups.</p><small>Candidate indicator</small><p><strong>Gender employment gap</strong></p></article><article class="ci-dimension"><span class="ci-dimension-number">04</span><h3>Welfare</h3><p>Income, poverty and living conditions.</p><small>Candidate indicator</small><p><strong>At-risk-of-poverty rate</strong></p></article><article class="ci-dimension"><span class="ci-dimension-number">05</span><h3>Sustainability</h3><p>Sustainable working lives, social resilience, and the social and solidarity economy.</p><small>Thematic pilot candidate</small><p><strong>Social economy share of paid employment</strong></p><a href="#social-economy">View the Türkiye pilot →</a></article><article class="ci-dimension"><span class="ci-dimension-number">06</span><h3>The future of work</h3><p>Digital skills, technological change and new forms of work.</p><small>Candidate indicator</small><p><strong>Basic or above-basic digital skills</strong></p></article></div></section>
<section id="social-economy" class="ci-sse" aria-labelledby="sse-title">
<div class="ci-section-heading"><div><p class="ci-eyebrow">TÜRKİYE PILOT / SUSTAINABILITY</p><h2 id="sse-title">Social economy and solidarity</h2><p>Investigating employment, organisational resilience and participation in organisations that put social purpose first.</p></div><span class="ci-sse-badge">Research design · not scored</span></div>
<p>Cooperatives, associations, foundations and social enterprises form a candidate research population. Inclusion requires an agreed operational definition informed by <a href="https://www.ilo.org/topics-and-sectors/social-and-solidarity-economy">ILO principles</a>; legal form alone does not establish eligibility.</p>
<div class="ci-sse-callout"><strong>No validated pilot values yet.</strong> These indicators are excluded from the overall score and country rankings. The synthetic explorer above does not measure social economy performance. Unavailable observations are not zeros.</div>
<div class="ci-sse-grid"><article class="ci-sse-card"><p class="ci-eyebrow">SSE-01 / Sustainability</p><h3>Social economy share of paid employment</h3><p class="ci-sse-state"><strong>Not collected / not validated</strong></p><p>Establish entity perimeter and obtain matching aggregate employment counts.</p><details><summary>Proposed measurement</summary><p><strong>Numerator:</strong> Annual average paid employee jobs in active entities meeting the pilot SSE definition.</p><p><strong>Denominator:</strong> Annual average paid employee jobs across the same domestic economy and year.</p><p>100 × numerator / denominator; same job-based unit and coverage in both terms.</p></details></article><article class="ci-sse-card"><p class="ci-eyebrow">SSE-02 / Sustainability</p><h3>Three-year social enterprise survival rate</h3><p class="ci-sse-state"><strong>Not collected / not validated</strong></p><p>Define births and activity; document mergers, closures, missing follow-up and changes in eligibility.</p><details><summary>Proposed measurement</summary><p><strong>Numerator:</strong> Eligible social enterprises born in year t and economically active in year t+3.</p><p><strong>Denominator:</strong> All eligible social enterprises born in year t in the observed birth cohort.</p><p>100 × numerator / denominator; administrative registration alone does not prove activity.</p></details></article><article class="ci-sse-card"><p class="ci-eyebrow">SSE-03 / Equality and inclusion</p><h3>Six-month paid employment retention among target-group entrants</h3><p class="ci-sse-state"><strong>Not collected / not validated</strong></p><p>Define target groups and follow-up protocol; report missing follow-up and response coverage.</p><details><summary>Proposed measurement</summary><p><strong>Numerator:</strong> Target-group entrants still in paid employment at an eligible entity six months after entry.</p><p><strong>Denominator:</strong> All target-group paid employment entrants in the same entry cohort with a full six-month observation window.</p><p>100 × numerator / denominator; report separately for each predefined target group; unknown follow-up remains unknown.</p></details></article><article class="ci-sse-card"><p class="ci-eyebrow">SSE-04 / Research panel</p><h3>Worker participation in organisational decisions</h3><p class="ci-sse-state"><strong>Not collected / not validated</strong></p><p>Pilot the question with workers; publish response rate, item non-response and sampling limitations.</p><details><summary>Proposed measurement</summary><p><strong>Numerator:</strong> Paid workers reporting access to and use of a defined participatory decision mechanism during the reference year.</p><p><strong>Denominator:</strong> Paid workers with valid responses to the same question in the pilot survey.</p><p>Weighted survey proportion only with a defensible sampling design; otherwise label as respondent-only descriptive results.</p></details></article></div>
<details class="ci-sse-details"><summary>What the first source review found</summary><ul><li><a href="https://ticaret.gov.tr/kooperatifcilik/bilgi-bankasi/illere-gore-kooperatif-dagilimi">Ministry of Trade:</a> the cooperative distribution page carries a 2026 update date but identifies the displayed table as June 2019. Publication and observation dates must be kept separate.</li><li><a href="https://www.siviltoplum.gov.tr/">Civil Society Relations:</a> association statistics are listed publicly; a usable paid-employment extract has not been verified.</li><li><a href="https://www.vgm.gov.tr/vakif-islemleri/vakif-istatistikleri/yeni-vakiflar">Foundations Directorate:</a> workforce-related tables are listed. Their PDF contents, periods and definitions still need validation before any figures are used.</li><li><a href="https://www.ilo.org/resource/news/advancing-global-statistical-framework-social-and-solidarity-economy">ILO statistical work</a> and <a href="https://www.oecd.org/content/dam/oecd/en/publications/reports/2024/06/insights-from-social-and-solidarity-economy-data_888cf72a/71d212f3-en.pdf">OECD research</a> guide the comparability review; a harmonised country series has not been established for this pilot.</li></ul><p>Source review: 4 November 2026. No institutional data agreement or access to restricted records is implied.</p></details>
<div class="ci-sse-downloads"><a href="assets/index/social-economy-indicators.csv" download>Indicator definitions and data gaps (CSV) ↓</a><a href="assets/index/social-economy-sources.csv" download>Source review register (CSV) ↓</a><a href="assets/index/social-economy-methodology.md" download>Pilot measurement protocol (English) ↓</a></div>
<p class="ci-table-note">Next milestone: agree the entity perimeter, validate source tables and statistical units, then collect a documented pilot dataset. No international social economy ranking will be produced before comparability is established.</p>
</section>
<section id="methodology" class="ci-method"><div><p class="ci-eyebrow">TRANSPARENT BY DESIGN</p><h2>From indicators to insight</h2><p>The Index aims to make developments measurable, comparable and trackable for researchers, decision-makers, public bodies and civil society.</p><a href="assets/index/indicator-candidates.csv" download>Download candidate indicator dictionary (CSV) ↓</a></div><div><ol><li><strong>Define the indicators.</strong> Confirm relevance, coverage and comparability with subject specialists.</li><li><strong>Document each observation.</strong> Record its source, unit, reference period, population and revision status.</li><li><strong>Agree the calculation.</strong> Publish direction, normalisation, weights, missing-data rules and sensitivity checks before releasing results.</li><li><strong>Publish reproducible results.</strong> Release versioned data, calculation rules and a methodology report together.</li></ol><p class="ci-method-note"><strong>Not yet decided:</strong> geographic coverage, baseline, indicator set, weighting and aggregation. The prototype’s 0–100 scores and equal weights are interface assumptions only. Missing values must never silently become zero.</p></div></section>
<section id="sources"><p class="ci-eyebrow">EVIDENCE BEFORE RANKINGS</p><h2>Planned institutional data sources</h2><p>The original brief identifies the institutions below. Their inclusion here does not imply a data agreement, verified indicator coverage or endorsement. The Working Life pilot uses the cited TÜİK release. The international demo uses no institutional observations. Social economy remains a source-review panel.</p><div class="ci-sources"><a href="https://www.tuik.gov.tr/">TurkStat (TÜİK) ↗</a><a href="https://www.sgk.gov.tr/">SGK ↗</a><a href="https://www.csgb.gov.tr/">ÇSGB ↗</a><a href="https://ilostat.ilo.org/">ILOSTAT ↗</a><a href="https://data-explorer.oecd.org/">OECD ↗</a><a href="https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat">Eurostat ↗</a><a href="https://data.worldbank.org/">World Bank ↗</a><a href="https://data.un.org/">United Nations ↗</a></div></section>
<footer class="ci-footer"><p><strong>A research programme in progress.</strong> The first Working Life observations are available. Next: extend job-quality coverage and agree the scoring methodology.</p><a href="iletisim.html">Contribute to the Index →</a></footer>
